title: Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of peace. What three? Peace of body, peace of speech, and peace of mind. Bhikkhus, these are the three…
content:
Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of peace. What three? Peace of body, peace of speech, and peace of mind. Bhikkhus, these are the three kinds of peace.

Peace of body, peace of speech,
Peace of mind, without taints,
One who is perfect in peace,
A sage, is called one who has washed away evil.

title: Bhikkhus, if while walking... while standing... while sitting... while lying down, thoughts of sensual desire, or thoughts of ill-will, or thoughts of harming arise in…
content: Bhikkhus, if while walking... while standing... while sitting... while lying down, thoughts of sensual desire, or thoughts of ill-will, or thoughts of harming arise in a bhikkhu, and if he accepts them, does not abandon them, does not dispel them, does not terminate them, does not make them nonexistent — then, bhikkhus, if while lying down, his consciousness behaves thus, he is called one who is not ardent, not conscientious, constantly lazy, of inferior energy.

title: Elder Bandhura: I have no need for this or that. I live happily, enjoying the taste of the Dhamma. Having drunk the supreme, first sweetness,…
content:
Elder Bandhura:

I have no need for this or that.
I live happily, enjoying the taste of the Dhamma.
Having drunk the supreme, first sweetness,
I will not associate with poison.

title: Rāhula, develop the development like space. Rāhula, by developing like space, agreeable and disagreeable contacts that arise do not take hold of the mind, do…
content: Rāhula, develop the development like space. Rāhula, by developing like space, agreeable and disagreeable contacts that arise do not take hold of the mind, do not remain. Rāhula, just as space is not established anywhere — so too, Rāhula, develop like space. Rāhula, by developing like space, agreeable and disagreeable contacts that arise do not take hold of the mind, do not remain.

title: Whoever checks the arising anger Like a chariot going straight, I call a charioteer. Others merely hold the reins. Conquer anger by non-anger, Conquer evil…
content:
Whoever checks the arising anger
Like a chariot going straight,
I call a charioteer.
Others merely hold the reins.

Conquer anger by non-anger,
Conquer evil by good,
Conquer stinginess by giving,
Conquer falsehood by truth.

Speak the truth, do not be angry,
When asked, give even from little.
By these three conditions,
One may go to the presence of the devas.

The wise do not harm anyone,
Their bodies are always restrained.
They go to the Deathless state,
Where there is no sorrow.

title: Just as, bhikkhus, a smith or his apprentice, when looking at his adze handle, sees the marks of his fingers and thumb. He cannot know:…
content: Just as, bhikkhus, a smith or his apprentice, when looking at his adze handle, sees the marks of his fingers and thumb. He cannot know: 'So much of my adze handle wore away today, so much yesterday, so much on other days.' But he knows it is wearing away by the wearing away itself. So too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who is devoted to development does not know: 'So much of my taints wore away today, so much yesterday, so much on other days.' But he knows they are wearing away by the wearing away itself. Just as, bhikkhus, a seafaring ship, fully rigged, stranded for six months due to lack of water in the dry season — its rigging gets damaged by wind and sun, then when the rains come, it becomes weak and rots. So too, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu who is devoted to development, the fetters easily weaken and rot.

title: - Wonderful, Venerable Sir! Wonderful, Venerable Sir! Just as one might set upright what had been overturned, reveal what had been hidden, show the way…
content: - Wonderful, Venerable Sir! Wonderful, Venerable Sir! Just as one might set upright what had been overturned, reveal what had been hidden, show the way to one who was lost, bring a lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes can see forms. So too, the Dhamma has been explained in many ways by the Blessed One. Venerable Sir, I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. May the Blessed One accept me as a lay follower, from today until the end of my life, I go for refuge.

title: Better than a thousand words That are meaningless, Is a single meaningful word, Upon hearing which, one becomes peaceful. Better than a thousand verses That…
content:
Better than a thousand words
That are meaningless,
Is a single meaningful word,
Upon hearing which, one becomes peaceful.

Better than a thousand verses
That are meaningless,
Is a single verse of meaning,
Upon hearing which, one becomes peaceful.

Better than reciting a hundred meaningless verses,
Is a single line of Dhamma,
Upon hearing which, one becomes peaceful.

title: - Bhikkhus, I will teach you nine things rooted in craving. Listen and pay close attention, I will speak. And, bhikkhus, what are the nine…
content: - Bhikkhus, I will teach you nine things rooted in craving. Listen and pay close attention, I will speak. And, bhikkhus, what are the nine things rooted in craving? Dependent on craving, seeking arises; dependent on seeking, gain arises; dependent on gain, decision arises; dependent on decision, desire and lust arises; dependent on desire and lust, attachment arises; dependent on attachment, possessiveness arises; dependent on possessiveness, stinginess arises; dependent on stinginess, guarding arises; from guarding, there arise the taking up of rods, the taking up of swords, quarrels, disputes, conflicts, divisive speech, false speech, and many other evil, unwholesome states. Bhikkhus, these are the nine things rooted in craving.

title: Questioner: From what do disputes and quarrels arise, Lamentation and sorrow, together with stinginess, Conceit and arrogance, along with divisive speech? From what do these…
content:
Questioner:
From what do disputes and quarrels arise,
Lamentation and sorrow, together with stinginess,
Conceit and arrogance, along with divisive speech?
From what do these many things arise? Please tell me.

The Blessed One:
From what is dear arise disputes and quarrels,
Lamentation and sorrow, together with stinginess,
Conceit and arrogance, along with divisive speech.
Disputes and quarrels are connected with stinginess;
Divisive speech arises from disputes.
